title: Verify silent blocking on physical Android and iPhone devices
summary: Run controlled real calls on both platforms and report whether silent blocking is actually supported before proceeding.
description:
CURRENT STATE: no real-device evidence yet establishes the no-disturbance requirement. P001/T001 measured entry capacity and P001/T002 inspected SDK contracts. Both remain completed historical work. This phase uses the probes/protocol prepared by P014/T019–T021. Runtime references are tools/entry-limit-harness/CallDir/CallDirectoryHandler.swift:20 and App/App.swift:42 on iOS; Android uses the ScreeningService.kt adapter planned by T021 beside MainActivity.kt:9, core/src/ffi.rs:309 and tools/build-android.sh:30. Production apps remain incomplete.

TASK OWNERSHIP: T022 verifies a physical Android phone; T023 verifies a physical iPhone. Each depends on both probe tasks, and transitively the protocol. Neither can begin before preparation is done and the user connects/authorizes the devices. There is no dependency between the two physical tasks; handset availability may change execution order. The task finishing second must consolidate the two platform verdicts before the phase is considered ready for user review.

PROTOCOL: record actual handset, OS, carrier, artifact/build, fixture alias, role/extension state and observation window. Establish a permitted call that visibly rings with Focus/silent mode, other blockers and native block lists controlled. Test the consented exact numbered caller with screen locked/unlocked and the app backgrounded/not visibly open. Verify block removal and return of normal calling. No ringtone, vibration, incoming UI or blocked/missed-call notification is acceptable; a call-record entry is acceptable. Observe delayed SMS/other alerts separately and classify their origin only where evidenced. A residual external disturbance requires an explicit conditional/failing result, not a clean full-silence claim; ask before changing carrier/system services.

PLATFORM FACTS: Android must actually invoke the screening service and receive its response within the SDK deadline; baseline callers are outside contacts with visible numbers. Notification suppression is distinct from silencing the ringtone; call-log suppression is not a reliable third-party control and is not required. iOS receives a preloaded exact-number list, gives no per-call callback/history API and offers no separate skip-notification switch. Successful loading is not evidence of silent real calls; observe the handset directly.

EVIDENCE AND STOP: persist redacted per-case pass/fail/blocked/not-tested results and cleanup/recovery evidence. Hardware absence or inconclusive cases are not passes. Report only the tested device/OS/carrier configurations. Do not add voicemail settings, SMS filtering, capacity stress tests or unrelated permissions/features. A completed investigation can report a failure, but must not mark the product requirement verified. Summarize both results and stop for the user's go/no-go before further app/core implementation; later production integration must repeat the tests.
goals: Measure whether blocked real calls cause any ringtone, vibration, incoming UI or blocked/missed-call notification on each physical platform.
Distinguish app/system behavior from delayed carrier SMS without assuming the latter can be controlled by the app.
Give the user a bounded cross-platform verdict and stop before further product implementation.
nonGoals: Guaranteeing behavior on untested device/OS/carrier combinations.
Treating records in the call log as a failure.
Silencing the whole phone, changing carrier services without permission, building voicemail settings, or disguising residual alerts with unrelated features.
Replacing later production-integration regression tests with probe evidence.
dependencies: All P014 preparation tasks (T019–T021) completed; enforced through task dependencies.
User-provided physical phones, approved installation/role/extension setup and consented real calling session.
risks: Physical phones may not yet be connected or authorized; this is waiting for user input, not a successful test.
The iPhone gives no per-call callback; a loaded block list cannot establish observed behavior.
Android screening exclusions or role loss may prevent the service from seeing a test call.
An OS or carrier may still create delayed alerts; report failure/conditional coverage and seek the user's decision instead of weakening acceptance.
openQuestions: Actual observed silent-blocking results on each handset/OS/carrier remain unknown.
Whether any carrier-generated missed-call message follows the block, and whether changing a carrier service would be required, remains unverified.
completionCriteria: T022 and T023 contain executed real-call evidence or explicit blocked/untested cases, with handset/OS/carrier/build identified.
Allowed-call controls ring before and after the block; screen/app-state cases and delayed-observation windows are recorded.
App/system alerts, permitted call records and carrier messages are reported separately; residual disturbance is not labeled a clean pass.

The platform verdicts and unresolved blockers are summarized for the user; any failure prevents declaring the no-disturbance requirement verified. Stop for user instructions before further implementation.

tasks.title: Verify no-disturbance blocking on a physical Android phone
tasks.description:
PHYSICAL EXECUTION ONLY AFTER PREPARATION: complete P014/T019, T020 and T021, then wait for the user to connect the phones and approve live calls. Read the protocol/result template produced under tools/device-tests/ and the exact Android probe/build instructions. Runtime references: apps/android/app/src/main/java/com/antoniopantano/callerfilter/MainActivity.kt:9, the ScreeningService.kt adapter created by T021, core/src/ffi.rs:309 and tools/build-android.sh:30. No Android device result exists yet.

RUN: identify the chosen handset, OS version, carrier, APK/build and fixture alias. Install with explicit device selection; obtain role approval from the user and verify ROLE_CALL_SCREENING. Keep the caller number presented and outside contacts. Record baseline ringtone/vibration/Focus settings, native block lists, other screening apps and relevant carrier services. First prove a permitted call rings. Then execute the protocol's exact blocked-number cases with locked/unlocked screen and the app backgrounded/not visibly open. Capture service invocation, core verdict and response timing alongside human observation; a log saying Block is not proof that the phone was undisturbed.

ACCEPTANCE: no ringtone, vibration, incoming UI, or blocked/missed-call notification. Logs/Recents entries are allowed; do not fail on them or rely on third-party suppression of the system call log. Observe the agreed window for delayed notifications/SMS. Record sender/time/content category with personal information redacted and separate carrier-generated effects from app/system behavior. A carrier-side disturbance is not silently excused as a full no-disturbance pass; ask the user before changing services and report any conditional result explicitly. Voicemail settings and Android SMS filtering remain out of scope.

CONTROL AND EVIDENCE: clear the test rule and verify the same number can ring again; record permission/role-loss behavior without using it to fake successful blocking. Record every planned case as pass/fail/blocked/not-tested, actual parameters and evidence paths. Missing hardware, denied permissions or inconclusive observations are not a pass. Preserve existing user data/settings and restore test-specific changes with the user's agreement. Publish bounded conclusions for the tested handset/OS/carrier only, with concrete remaining risks. These are platform probes; production integration must repeat the tests. Do not proceed to unrelated app/core work on completion.

checklist.title: Record the physical handset/OS/carrier/build, obtain installation/role approval and verify a ringing positive control.
Run the blocked-call matrix and correlate visible behavior with service/verdict/timing evidence.
Observe delayed app/system/carrier alerts and document any residual disturbance or untested case.
Clear the test rule, prove normal calling returns, and persist a redacted verdict with evidence and cleanup notes.

tasks.title: Verify no-disturbance blocking on a physical iPhone
tasks.description:
PHYSICAL EXECUTION ONLY AFTER PREPARATION: complete P014/T019, T020 and T021, then wait for the user to connect the phones and approve live calls. Use the common protocol/result template under tools/device-tests/ and the prepared iPhone probe. References: tools/entry-limit-harness/CallDir/CallDirectoryHandler.swift:20, App/App.swift:42, run.sh:12 and README.md:1. P001/T001 measured capacity on one iPhone; it did not establish that a real blocked call produces no notification or other disturbance.

RUN: record the actual iPhone model, iOS version, carrier, signed build and fixture alias. Select this device explicitly; have the user complete pairing, trust/Developer Mode and Call Directory enablement as required. Confirm the exact-number fixture was accepted by the extension and record enabled state/reload outcome. Establish that an unblocked control call visibly rings with Focus/silent mode and other blocking/screening features controlled and recorded. Run the exact blocked-number cases with screen locked/unlocked and the app backgrounded/not visibly open.

EVIDENCE LIMIT: Call Directory loads entries in advance and gives the app no per-call callback or call-history API. Do not infer a blocked-call event from extension logs, fabricate a history, or treat successful reload as proof of silence. Observe the actual screen, sound/vibration and notification center during the call and throughout the protocol's delayed-observation window; user-provided recordings/screenshots/notes may supply that evidence.

ACCEPTANCE: no ringtone, vibration, incoming-call UI, or blocked/missed-call notification. Recents/call-log entries are acceptable. Record any unsolicited SMS or other delayed alert and its evidenced origin separately. The probe cannot issue a separate skip-notification setting or disable a carrier missed-call service. If an alert remains, report failed/conditional/unverified coverage rather than promising that all iPhones are silent. Ask before any user/carrier setting change; no voicemail-settings feature or SMS-filter workaround is authorized.

CONTROL AND CLOSE: clear the fixture/reload or use the documented empty-list control and prove the same caller can ring again. Redact personal numbers/identifiers in committed evidence, preserve private raw artifacts separately, restore test changes with consent and record every case as pass/fail/blocked/not-tested. At the end of P017 reconcile both platform verdicts and stop for the user's go/no-go decision before further implementation. Completion with evidence does not mean every case passed. Production app integration must repeat the tests.

Incoming-call UI and the complete settings matrix were not separately reported. This establishes reported baseline channels, NOT a completed matrix or a silence pass. Then observe actual blocked calls including the Watch, missed notifications and NEW SMS; baseline SMS must not be confused with later alerts. Carrier, SMS origin, full settings/timing evidence, answered controls, repeated denies across all required screen/app states and empty recovery remain outstanding. Retain the signed empty artifact for recovery. All no-disturbance claims remain unverified; do not complete this task from installation/reload or incomplete baseline evidence.
